d5_d4_nl_di_advanced_ene_spi_o10_o11_o14.proposition: Taken together, A and B extend and corroborate the durability distinction already drawn between the two hosts. A established that the host with the more favorable chemistry/morphology/overpotential profile (associated with CnC HS) also survives far longer at stable CE than the other host (which collapsed to zero CE by about 40-48 cycles and had no data past ~50 cycles), while CnC HS held roughly 93-100% CE out to about 205 cycles. B adds a further, independent stability read on that same better-performing side of the pair, carried out to 500 cycles: charge/discharge capacity only falls from about 1.0 to about 0.9 mAh over that span, and the voltage profile at the 1st and 100th cycle nearly overlap. Combined, this shows the favorable host's stability is not confined to the ~205-cycle CE window already documented but continues, by a second metric (capacity retention and profile shape), out to 500 cycles -- i.e. the two measurements corroborate one another on durability using different metrics and a longer horizon, reinforcing rather than merely repeating the earlier divergence.
limits: Does not identify which structural/chemical feature (nitrogen chemistry vs. flatter/denser morphology) drives either the earlier CE divergence or this capacity retention -- that confound from the earlier result is unchanged and unresolved by adding B.

The two measurements are different kinds of quantity: A's cycling result is a percentage-CE endurance/failure record tracked to a cycle count (~205 cycles for the better host, collapse by ~40-48 cycles for the other), while B is an absolute capacity amount in mAh tracked as a fade curve over 500 cycles plus a qualitative profile-overlap check at only two cycle numbers (1st and 100th). No shared scale lets the size of the CE divergence be compared to the size of the ~1.0-to-0.9 mAh capacity fade.

B's profile-overlap claim is anchored at only two specific cycles (1st and 100th) within the 500-cycle window, so it supports early-cycle shape stability, not a claim about the full 500-cycle trajectory of the profile.

Still only a two-material comparison; B does not add a new host or intermediate case, only a longer/second measurement on the side already favored in A, so this remains a co-occurrence between two endpoints rather than a dose-response or multi-point relationship.
Neither observation nor their combination speaks to a stacked-cell or device-level outcome; both are single-cell measurements.
d5_d4_nl_di_advanced_ene_spi_o10_o11_o14.not_identifiable: nitrogen chemical-environment change vs. flatter/more compact zinc morphology, as drivers of the extended cycling/capacity stability shown across A and B

d5_d4_nl_di_advanced_ene_spi_o10_o11_o14.proposition: Read together, the CE-cycling divergence already tied to CnC HS vs C HS (A) and the functional demonstration of a cell stack powering a switched-on mobile phone (B) establish that the host material identified as the more durable one in cycling (the one holding stable CE out to about 205 cycles, unlike C HS which collapsed to zero by about 40-48 cycles) is also the material whose cell stack succeeds in delivering usable power to a real load. The pairing bridges a cycle-count electrochemical stability metric with a practical, device-level power-delivery capability for the same material line -- a link neither observation makes by itself.
limits: B is a single, one-time functional demonstration: the observation states only that the phone is switched on while powered by the stack; it reports no cycle count, no duration, and no capacity/voltage trace for that stack, so it cannot on its own show durability.

A alone reports CE percentage over cycle number in what is a cycling-stability measurement, not a load-powering test; it does not by itself show that this stability translates into the ability to run a real device.

The confound already present in A -- nitrogen chemical-environment change versus flatter/more compact morphology as the driver of the CE divergence -- is inherited unchanged; combining with B does nothing to resolve which of those two co-occurring properties, if either, underlies anything, including B's demonstrated functionality.

The two observations are a single co-occurrence (one material pairing, one device demo), not a series of points, so no dose-response or graded relationship between degree of CE stability and degree of device-powering capability can be drawn.
Nothing here generalizes beyond the one demonstrated device/load; the pairing does not establish service capability across other loads, durations, or repeated device tests.
d5_d4_nl_di_advanced_ene_spi_o10_o11_o14.not_identifiable: Whether the phone-powering capability shown in B depends on (is caused by) the long-term CE cycling stability established in A, versus simply reflects sufficient instantaneous capacity/voltage output at a single time point independent of cycling durability, cannot be separated using only these two observations.

So the combination supports that the long-cycling stability advantage documented for CnC HS corresponds to an actual working, load-bearing power source rather than being confined to the symmetric-cell test alone.

Mismatched quantity kinds: A is a cumulative time-course of voltage stability over minutes of cycling (stable to about 7100 min for CnC HS vs. spikes from about 2600 min and failure near 4400 min for C HS); B is a one-off functional/capability reading (multimeter confirms a phone is powered), not a rate, amount, or duration -- no dose-response or duration-matching between the two can be drawn.

Different cell configurations: A's stability data come from symmetric two-electrode cells, while B's demonstration is a multi-cell stack; scaling the symmetric-cell durability figures onto the stack's practical performance is not established.

Inherits A's own qualifications: A itself does not identify which of the chemistry, morphology, or overpotential differences (or an unmeasured host difference) causes the stability divergence, so even the 'stability advantage' half of this combination remains a co-occurrence, not a demonstrated cause of the phone-powering result.
d5_d4_nl_di_advanced_ene_spi_o10_o11_o14.not_identifiable: Whether the successful phone-powering demonstration reflects the CnC HS stability advantage established in A, versus simply reflecting that the stack had sufficient voltage/capacity at the moment of testing independent of long-term cycling stability, cannot be separated -- B provides no C HS comparison and no durability data of its own.
